Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/mcp

# DeepLinkNow MCP server for coding agents

## Overview

[`@deeplinknow/mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp) is an MCP server for coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Windsurf. With it installed, the agent can read DeepLinkNow's current docs, check your link domain and plan a migration while it writes the integration, instead of working from memory.

It covers iOS, Android, React Native, Expo and Flutter apps. Like DeepLinkNow itself, it does deep linking only: it never adds attribution, ad tracking or advertising IDs to your app.

The server runs on your machine over stdio and needs Node.js 20 or later. The source is MIT licensed: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp).

## Install

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add deeplinknow -- npx -y @deeplinknow/mcp
```

With the link tools (`--scope user` keeps the key out of the project's `.mcp.json`):

```sh
claude mcp add deeplinknow --scope user --env DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY=YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY -- npx -y @deeplinknow/mcp
```

### Cursor

Add to `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "${env:DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `env` if you don't need the link tools.

### Claude Desktop

Open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**, which opens `claude_desktop_config.json` (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\Claude\` on Windows), and add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop. To use the link tools, add `"env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY" }` next to `args`.

### VS Code

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks for the key once and stores it securely:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "deeplinknow-api-key",
      "description": "DeepLinkNow private API key (dln_priv_…), only for list_links and create_link. Leave empty otherwise.",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "${input:deeplinknow-api-key}" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Windsurf

Add to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deeplinknow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@deeplinknow/mcp"],
      "env": { "DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY": "YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

Leave out `env` if you don't need the link tools.

### Other clients

Any MCP client that runs stdio servers: command `npx`, arguments `-y @deeplinknow/mcp`.

## What to ask

```text
Add DeepLinkNow deferred deep linking to this app. Our link domain is myapp.deeplinknow.com.
```

The agent reads the setup guide for your platform, installs the SDK, adds the Associated Domains entitlement and the Android intent filter, calls `checkDeferredDeepLink()` on launch and routes the result through your router. Then it checks your domain.

Other requests it handles:

- "Check myapp.deeplinknow.com" (or your custom domain). It validates `apple-app-site-association` against Apple's CDN copy and `assetlinks.json` against Google's Digital Asset Links API, and looks the domain up on the EasyPrivacy and AdGuard block lists. It works for any domain, including the one you use today.
- "We're on Firebase Dynamic Links. Move us to DeepLinkNow." Branch, AppsFlyer and Adjust work too. You get a plan and a code diff for your platform. If you use one of those for attribution, the plan keeps it for that and moves only the deep links.
- "This match came back MEDIUM with a score of 58. Should we route it?" The agent explains each part of the score and what a `minConfidence` of 50 or 75 would do. The threshold stays your decision.

## Tools

| Tool | Needs a key | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `get_setup_guide` | No | Setup steps and code for `ios`, `android`, `react-native`, `expo` or `flutter`, from these docs (a bundled copy when offline) |
| `search_docs` | No | Searches the full DeepLinkNow docs and returns the matching sections with links |
| `check_domain` | No | Checks a domain's `apple-app-site-association` (and Apple's CDN copy), `assetlinks.json` (and Google's verdict), and whether the domain or its CNAME chain is on the EasyPrivacy or AdGuard block lists |
| `explain_match_result` | No | Explains a fingerprint match's `confidence_score` and `match_quality`, and how to choose `minConfidence` |
| `migrate_from` | No | A migration plan and code diff from `firebase-dynamic-links`, `branch`, `appsflyer` or `adjust` |
| `list_links` | Private key, paid plan | Lists the app's links (dashboard, API and on-demand), with search and paging |
| `create_link` | Private key, paid plan | Creates a link with a custom path, link-page text, social preview, metadata or campaign |

It also exposes `deeplinknow://llms.txt` and `deeplinknow://docs/{page}` as resources, and two prompts: `add_deferred_deep_linking` and `migrate_to_deeplinknow`.

The first `check_domain` run downloads the block lists (about 22 MB). Later checks in the same session reuse them for a day.

## Keys

You don't need an account or a key for the first five tools.

`list_links` and `create_link` call the [management API](/docs/api/deeplinks), which needs your app's **private** key (`dln_priv_…`, from the app's API Keys page in the dashboard) as `DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY`. The management API is on paid plans ([pricing](/pricing)). A private key acts on one app.

You never have to create links: any path on your link domain already works. The link tools are for listing links, or for creating one with a custom preview or campaign.

The private key stays in your MCP config. Your app only ever contains the public key (`dln_pub_…`). The server refuses a public key for the link tools without sending it, and it never prints, logs or returns the private key: it sends it only in the `x-api-key` header to the DeepLinkNow API.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEEPLINKNOW_API_KEY` | unset | Your app's private key, only for `list_links` and `create_link` |
| `DEEPLINKNOW_API_URL` | `https://deeplinknow.com` | API base URL. Must be https (http only for localhost) |

## What it doesn't do

- **It never writes files or runs commands.** The server only returns text to the agent. Your agent makes the code changes, through its own tools and permission prompts.
- **It stores nothing on disk.** Docs, block lists and check results are cached in memory while the server runs (docs for an hour, block lists for a day, domain results for 5 minutes).
- **No telemetry.** It collects no usage data.
- **It sends nothing about your code.** `get_setup_guide`, `search_docs`, `migrate_from` and the resources fetch public docs from `https://deeplinknow.com`. `check_domain` fetches only the domain you name (over https, refusing private and local addresses), Apple's CDN, Google's Digital Asset Links API and the four public block lists. `explain_match_result` makes no requests. Only the link tools send your key and the link fields, to the DeepLinkNow API.

## Keep agents on track

Paste this into your repo's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` so every session follows the same rules:

```markdown
## Deep linking: DeepLinkNow

- Link domain: myapp.deeplinknow.com. Any path and query on it is a deep link; nothing has to be created first.
- The app contains only the public key (dln_pub_…). Never commit or ship the private key.
- Initialize once at launch. Call checkDeferredDeepLink() once on launch and route to link.path with link.queryParams. Send links that open the installed app through the SDK's parse method and the same router.
- Fingerprint matches are scored (confidenceScore, matchQuality). minConfidence is off by default; decide how to treat MEDIUM and LOW.
- Use the DeepLinkNow MCP tools (get_setup_guide, check_domain, search_docs) instead of guessing.
```

## Support

- Email: support@deeplinknow.com
- Package: [npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deeplinknow/mcp)
- Source: [github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp](https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-mcp)

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/firebase-migration

# Migrating from Firebase Dynamic Links

Firebase Dynamic Links shut down on 25 August 2025: every `page.link` URL now returns a 404, and the `.page.link` domains are gone. Nobody can bring those URLs back, DeepLinkNow included. This guide moves the *behaviour* to DeepLinkNow: links that open your app if it's installed, survive an install if it isn't, and hand your app the original link on first launch.

There are two ways to do it. Pick one, or start with the first and move to the second over time.

## Option 1: keep your long links, change the host

If you built Dynamic Links in code as long links, like

```
https://yourapp.page.link/?link=https%3A%2F%2Fyourapp.com%2Finvite%2F8Fk2&apn=com.yourapp&ibi=com.yourapp.ios
```

the same URL works on your DeepLinkNow domain with only the host changed:

```
https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/?link=https%3A%2F%2Fyourapp.com%2Finvite%2F8Fk2&apn=com.yourapp&ibi=com.yourapp.ios
```

DeepLinkNow accepts any path and query on your domain without creating links first, and passes the query through untouched. Your app gets the Firebase-style `link` parameter back, already decoded, in `queryParams.link`, both when the link opens the installed app and after an install.

All long links on `/` count as **one** link against your plan's link limit, because the limit counts distinct paths and ignores the query string.

What's different from Firebase:

- `apn`, `ibi`, `isi` and `efr` aren't needed. DeepLinkNow knows your app from the domain, and it sends users to the App Store or Google Play listing you set in the dashboard. They're harmless to leave in.
- `afl`, `ifl` and `ofl` (fallback URLs) aren't followed. Phones go to the store; desktop shows a QR code and store buttons.
- `st`, `sd` and `si` (social preview) aren't read from the URL. Set the preview title, description and image in the dashboard (paid plans).
- Short links (`yourapp.page.link/abc`) have no equivalent code to keep: use a path instead (Option 2).

### React Native

Before (`@react-native-firebase/dynamic-links`):

```typescript
const initial = await dynamicLinks().getInitialLink();
if (initial) handle(initial.url);
dynamicLinks().onLink((link) => handle(link.url));
```

After (`@deeplinknow/react-native`):

```typescript
import DeepLinkNow from "@deeplinknow/react-native";
import { Linking } from "react-native";

await DeepLinkNow.initialize("dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx");

const linkParam = (q: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  typeof q.link === "string" ? q.link : null;

// After an install: the link the user tapped before installing.
const deferred = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink();
const fromInstall = deferred && linkParam(deferred.queryParams);
if (fromInstall) handle(fromInstall);

// App already installed: the Universal Link / App Link that opened it.
const onUrl = (url: string | null) => {
  const parsed = url ? DeepLinkNow.parseDeepLink(url) : null;
  const value = parsed && linkParam(parsed.queryParams);
  if (value) handle(value);
};
Linking.getInitialURL().then(onUrl);
Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => onUrl(url));
```

### iOS (Swift)

```swift
import DeepLinkNow

await DeepLinkNow.initialize(config: DLNConfig(apiKey: "dln_pub_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"))

// After an install
if let deferred = await DeepLinkNow.checkDeferredDeepLink(),
   let value = deferred.queryParams["link"]?.stringValue {
    handle(URL(string: value))
}

// App already installed (SwiftUI)
.onOpenURL { url in
    if let link = DeepLinkNow.parseLink(url),
       let value = link.queryParams["link"]?.stringValue {
        handle(URL(string: value))
    }
}
```

### Android (Kotlin)

```kotlin
// After an install (inside a coroutine; it returns a Result and never throws)
DLN.checkDeferredDeepLink().onSuccess { deferred ->
    (deferred?.queryParams?.get("link") as? QueryValue.Single)?.value?.let(::handle)
}

// App already installed (onCreate and onNewIntent)
intent.data?.toString()?.let { url ->
    DLN.parseDeepLink(url)?.let { link ->
        (link.queryParams["link"] as? QueryValue.Single)?.value?.let(::handle)
    }
}
```

## Option 2: put the path in the link

Firebase needed the `link=` wrapper because `page.link` wasn't your domain. On DeepLinkNow it is. Instead of wrapping `https://yourapp.com/invite/8Fk2`, use the path directly:

```
https://yourapp.deeplinknow.com/invite/8Fk2
```

Your app gets `path: "/invite/8Fk2"` and any query parameters, and routes on them. This is shorter, reads better in a message, and works with your own domain (`go.yourapp.com/invite/8Fk2`) on paid plans.

Each distinct path counts once against your link limit, so put per-user values in the query (`/invite?code=8Fk2`) if you generate a lot of them.

## Checklist

1. Create the app in the DeepLinkNow dashboard and enter your iOS Team ID and Bundle ID and your Android package name and SHA-256 fingerprints. DeepLinkNow serves `apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json` for your domain.
2. Add `applinks:yourapp.deeplinknow.com` to Associated Domains (iOS) and an `autoVerify` https intent filter for it (Android). With Expo, the config plugin does both.
3. Replace the Firebase Dynamic Links SDK calls as shown above, and remove the `firebase_dynamic_links` / `@react-native-firebase/dynamic-links` dependency.
4. Change the host in the code that builds links (Option 1), or switch to paths (Option 2).
5. Check your domain with the free [deep link domain checker](/tools).

## What DeepLinkNow doesn't replace

- **Old `page.link` URLs.** They're dead. Update links you control (emails, QR codes, your site), and accept that old shared links won't open.
- **Firebase Auth email-link sign-in.** It used Dynamic Links for the sign-in email; Firebase's own documentation covers moving that flow off Dynamic Links. DeepLinkNow doesn't handle sign-in links.
- **Analytics.** Firebase reported clicks into Google Analytics. DeepLinkNow shows click and install counts, and hands your app the link so you can send it to your own analytics.

---
Source: https://deeplinknow.com/docs/integration-checklist

# Integration Checklist

An end-to-end checklist for integrating DeepLinkNow into your mobile app.

## Dashboard setup

### Account and app

- [ ] Create a DeepLinkNow account and an app in the dashboard
- [ ] Choose your app alias (e.g. `myapp` → `myapp.deeplinknow.com`)
- [ ] Copy your keys from the **API Keys** page. Each app gets one **public** key (`dln_pub_…`, for the SDKs) and one **private** key (`dln_priv_…`, for your server only). The public key is always shown there. The private key is shown once; regenerate it there if you lose it, and choose how long the old one keeps working (24 hours by default, or immediately if it leaked).
- [ ] Optional: configure a fallback URL for desktop visitors

### iOS settings

- [ ] Bundle ID (e.g. `com.company.myapp`)
- [ ] Team ID / App ID prefix (from your Apple Developer account)
- [ ] App Store ID (once the app is published)

### Android settings

- [ ] Package name (e.g. `com.company.myapp`)
- [ ] SHA-256 certificate fingerprints: Play App Signing, upload key and debug (`keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore`)

### Verify the .well-known files

- [ ] `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` contains your Team ID and Bundle ID
- [ ] `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json` contains your package name and fingerprints

These files are served from your saved settings and cached for up to 5 minutes.

## SDK installation

- [ ] **React Native / Expo**: `npx expo install @deeplinknow/react-native` (development build, not Expo Go) or `npm install @deeplinknow/react-native` + `pod install`
- [ ] **iOS**: `pod 'DeepLinkNow', '~> 1.3'` or Swift Package Manager `https://github.com/deeplinknow/dln-ios`
- [ ] **Android**: `implementation("com.deeplinknow:dln-android:1.3.0")` (the library declares `INTERNET` itself)
- [ ] **Flutter**: `flutter pub add deeplinknow` (iOS 13+, Android `minSdk` 24; rebuild the app after adding it)
- [ ] iOS: Associated Domains `applinks:myapp.deeplinknow.com` (and your custom domain)
- [ ] Android: `autoVerify` https intent filter for `myapp.deeplinknow.com` (and your custom domain)
- [ ] No ATT prompt, IDFA, or advertising-ID permission is needed for DeepLinkNow

## Initialization

- [ ] Initialize once at app start with your **public** key (`dln_pub_…`)
- [ ] Never ship your private key in an app
- [ ] Handle an initialization failure (invalid key, inactive account, offline) separately from "no deferred link"
- [ ] Use `enableLogs` only in development builds

## Deferred deep linking

- [ ] Call `checkDeferredDeepLink()` once on launch, after initialization
- [ ] Route to `link.path` with `link.queryParams` when it returns a link
- [ ] Decide your threshold for fingerprint results. Every result carries `confidenceScore` (0–100) and `matchQuality` (`HIGH` 75+, `MEDIUM` 50–74, `LOW` 30–49). The optional `minConfidence` filter is off by default.
- [ ] Consider confirming `MEDIUM` or `LOW` fingerprint matches with the user before routing
- [ ] iOS: decide whether to keep the pasteboard step (`useClipboard`, default `true`), which can show the iOS 16+ paste prompt
- [ ] Treat errors as "try again later", not as "no link". The SDK retries on the next call.

## Links that open the installed app

- [ ] Pass incoming Universal Links / App Links to `parseDeepLink(url)`
- [ ] Route deferred and direct links through the same function

```typescript
function route(path: string, query: Record<string, string | true | string[]>) {
  switch (path) {
    case "/product":
      navigation.navigate("Product", { id: query.id });
      break;
    case "/category":
      navigation.navigate("Category", { name: query.name });
      break;
    default:
      navigation.navigate("Home");
  }
}
```

- [ ] Handle unknown paths gracefully

## Testing

### Direct links

- [ ] Tap `https://myapp.deeplinknow.com/product?id=123` from Notes or Messages with the app installed: the app opens on the right screen
- [ ] Android: `adb shell pm get-app-links <your.package>` shows your domains as verified

### Deferred links

- [ ] Uninstall the app, tap a link, install, open: the app lands on the right screen
- [ ] iOS: test both **Allow** and **Don't Allow** on the paste prompt (Don't Allow falls back to fingerprint matching)
- [ ] Android: test an install through the link's Play Store button (Install Referrer) and one without it (fingerprint)
- [ ] Check the logs for each step's outcome, `source`, `confidenceScore` and `matchQuality`
- [ ] Use `resetDeferredDeepLink()` or `force: true` to repeat the test without reinstalling
- [ ] A click older than 1 hour is not offered as a fingerprint match

### Edge cases

- [ ] First launch offline: no crash, and the next launch still finds the link
- [ ] Unknown path: falls back to a sensible screen
- [ ] A link copied from another app's domain is ignored

## Production readiness

- [ ] Only the public key is in the app binary
- [ ] Logging is off in release builds
- [ ] `.well-known` files are correct for your release signing certificates
- [ ] Privacy labels: the SDKs collect device characteristics and an app-scoped install ID for app functionality only, not for tracking

## Optional

- [ ] Custom domain (paid plans): add it under **Domains**, create the DNS record, wait for verification, then add it to Associated Domains and your intent filters
- [ ] Customize the landing page (title, subtitle, button text, social preview)
- [ ] Forward deferred-link events to your own analytics tool (DeepLinkNow does not do analytics)

## Need Help?

- [Quick Start](/docs/quickstart)
- [iOS](/docs/ios), [Android](/docs/android), [React Native](/docs/react-native), [Flutter](/docs/flutter)
- [MCP server for coding agents](/docs/mcp)
- Email: support@deeplinknow.com

# DeepLinkNow pricing

Prices in USD. Startup and Growth are billed monthly: cancel any time, and paid plans keep their features until the end of the billing period. Enterprise is billed annually, by invoice.
No free trial is needed: the Developer plan is free, with no card.

## Developer: $0/month

Deep links and deferred deep links for one app, free.

- 25k SDK monthly active users
- 1k deep links (distinct paths, on-demand included)
- Single app on yourapp.deeplinknow.com
- Just you (1 seat)
- Universal Links, App Links and deferred deep links
- iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter SDKs
- Click and install counts
- Community support on Discord

## Startup: $49/month

Your own domain and a landing page that looks like your app.

- 100k SDK monthly active users
- 10k deep links (distinct paths, on-demand included)
- Custom domains: your links on go.yourapp.com (up to 3)
- Up to 3 apps
- Up to 3 team members, with admin and member roles
- Your branding on the link page, not ours
- Custom link page text and buttons, per app or per link
- Custom social previews for iMessage, Slack, WhatsApp and more
- Link page translated into 14 languages
- Link rules: allowed paths and a not-found redirect
- Android: skip the link page, straight to Google Play
- Management API (10k requests/mo)
- Email support

## Growth: $149/month

For larger apps, or several apps under one account.

- 500k SDK monthly active users
- 50k deep links (distinct paths, on-demand included)
- Unlimited custom domains
- Unlimited apps
- Up to 5 team members
- Everything in Startup
- Management API (50k requests/mo)
- Email support

## Enterprise: Starting at $500/month, billed annually

For companies whose IT, legal and procurement teams have to sign off.

- Everything in Growth
- Custom MAU, link and API volume, including per-minute rate limits
- Pay by invoice, against your purchase order
- Unlimited team members
- Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace, and SSO required for your domain
- Audit log of who changed what in your workspace (coming soon)
- Data processing agreement (DPA)
- Priority support

## Attribution platforms

Measurement platforms with deep links inside. If you need attribution, these are the real choice. If you don't, you pay for it anyway, in money, advertising IDs or both.

- [DeepLinkNow vs Branch](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/branch.md): Branch dropped its free tier. Custom domains start at $199/mo.
- [DeepLinkNow vs AppsFlyer](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/appsflyer.md): No deferred deep links on the free plan. Paid tiers need a sales call.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Adjust](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/adjust.md): Attribution first. Deferred links may be limited after an ATT opt-out.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Singular](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/singular.md): Free to 15,000 paid conversions. Every deep link is an attribution link.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Kochava](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/kochava.md): Free attribution with deferred links. Universal Links and your domain start at $500/mo.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Airbridge](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/airbridge.md): An MMP from $40/mo. Your deferred link waits on the ATT prompt.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Linkrunner](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/linkrunner.md): A low-cost MMP, free to 25,000 attributed installs. It reads advertising IDs.

## Developer-first deep linking tools

Smaller tools that do deep links without the full attribution suite, most of them started after Firebase Dynamic Links shut down. Several of them start cheaper than I do, and the pages say so.

- [DeepLinkNow vs Detour](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/detour.md): 1,500 free clicks, custom domains at $79/mo, and no match score in the app.
- [DeepLinkNow vs ChottuLink](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/chottulink.md): The same 25,000 MAU free tier as mine, cheaper paid plans, and links you create first.
- [DeepLinkNow vs WarpLink](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/warplink.md): Strong tooling, billed per click, and no iOS clipboard step.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Dynalinks](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/dynalinks.md): No deferred links on the free plan. Pro is $14.99 per project.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Flinku](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/flinku.md): Catch-all routing from $12/mo. Past the click cap, links stop redirecting.
- [DeepLinkNow vs Rift](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/rift.md): Cheap and new. No fingerprint fallback, no React Native SDK.
- [DeepLinkNow vs LinkTrace](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/linktrace.md): $9.99 to start, no SDK, fingerprint only. Universal Links need the $29.99 plan.
- [DeepLinkNow vs AppsOnAir](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/appsonair.md): AppLink is a paid module from $34.98/mo, and a custom domain is $19.99 more.
- [DeepLinkNow vs URLgenius](https://deeplinknow.com/compare/urlgenius.md): Billed per click. Deferred links start at $199/mo on its Custom plan.

- [Firebase Dynamic Links alternative](https://deeplinknow.com/firebase-dynamic-links-alternative): Google shut it down on August 25, 2025. What DeepLinkNow does in its place, and what it doesn't.

# DeepLinkNow vs Branch

Deep linking and attribution platform. Facts as of October 19, 2026, each with a public source.

I used Branch on a real startup. It worked, mostly, until the bill and the ad blockers showed up. Branch is a fine product if you're a marketing team that wants attribution and campaign analytics. If you just want a link to open the right screen after install, you're paying for a lot you'll never open.

| | DeepLinkNow | Branch | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | None. A 30-day trial needs a work email and a card, then moves to Intro at $39/mo. | [1] [2] |
| Usage over the plan | Links and SDK calls keep working. I'll ask you to upgrade. | Billed per extra volume credit, link and click, uncapped. | [3] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Activation Basics, $199/mo | [4] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | Included on every plan, free one too | NativeLink, a premium feature | [5] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created in the dashboard or API, or long links with /a/key_live_… on a custom domain. Routing by path needs $deeplink_path and custom logic. | [6] [7] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | Collected by default (FULL protection level: advertising IDs and device IDs) | [8] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | Branch domains and its web SDK are on AdGuard and EasyPrivacy, and EasyPrivacy blocks about 4,195 Branch customer link domains. | [9] [10] |
| Typical contract | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Median about $55K a year (Vendr, 61 deals) | [11] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block list checkers, no sign-up needed.

## Pick Branch if…

- You need attribution, ad network integrations and campaign analytics, and someone else's budget pays for it.
- You want Journeys web banners and a marketing team running links without developers.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Branch's Intro plan is $39 a month with 5,000 volume credits, 500 links or QR codes and 25,000 clicks. Past that it bills $0.01 a click, $0.05 a link and $0.05 a volume credit, with no cap. I bill on monthly active users instead. [1] [3]

Say your links get 40,000 clicks a month. On Intro that's $39 plus 15,000 extra clicks at $0.01, so $189 before any volume-credit overage, and still no custom domain. On DeepLinkNow it's free while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users and 1,000 distinct paths, or $49 on Startup with your own domain. If your links get under 25,000 clicks and you don't need a custom domain, Intro's $39 is closer to my price than this example suggests.

## Switching from Branch

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Branch SDK in the next release.

## Questions

### How does Branch's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Branch's Intro plan is $39 a month with 5,000 volume credits, 500 links or QR codes and 25,000 clicks. Past that it bills $0.01 a click, $0.05 a link and $0.05 a volume credit, with no cap. I bill on monthly active users instead. Say your links get 40,000 clicks a month. On Intro that's $39 plus 15,000 extra clicks at $0.01, so $189 before any volume-credit overage, and still no custom domain. On DeepLinkNow it's free while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users and 1,000 distinct paths, or $49 on Startup with your own domain. If your links get under 25,000 clicks and you don't need a custom domain, Intro's $39 is closer to my price than this example suggests.

### When is Branch the better choice?

You need attribution, ad network integrations and campaign analytics, and someone else's budget pays for it. You want Journeys web banners and a marketing team running links without developers.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Branch?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Adjust

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Adjust is an attribution platform. Its deep linking product, TrueLink, sits inside it: links are created in Campaign Lab or the API, the SDK collects advertising IDs, and Adjust's own docs say deferred deep linking may be limited for users who opt out of tracking. I couldn't check its prices: the pricing page turned away automated requests on the day I looked.

| | DeepLinkNow | Adjust | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deferred deep linking | Included on every plan, free one too | In TrueLink Base. The deep link generator API and the faster ODDL path need TrueLink Core or Enterprise. | [1] [9] |
| Published prices | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | None I could check. Vendr's buyers report a median of $44,000 a year (31 deals), from $10,800 to $370,080. | [8] |
| After an ATT opt-out | Nothing changes. No advertising IDs are involved. | "Deferred deep linking may be limited for users that opt-out." | [2] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | Included on every plan, free one too | LinkMe: iOS 15 and up, SDK 4.31.0, and only if the user is in Safari | [3] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created in Campaign Lab or through the API, as short links on yourbrand.go.link/<token> | [4] [5] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | A branded name in front of .go.link, which can't be changed after you save it | [5] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | The Android SDK adds the AD_ID permission by default. The iOS SDK's privacy manifest declares tracking, with eight tracking domains. | [6] [7] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | adj.st, the legacy link domain, is on AdGuard Tracking Protection, and app.adjust.com is on EasyPrivacy | [10] [11] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Published prices: $0, $49 or $149 a month. You only talk to me if you want Enterprise.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Adjust if…

- You buy ads and need attribution, including SKAdNetwork when users opt out of tracking.

Sources: [2] [12]

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Adjust bills on attributions. Its live pricing page refused automated requests on October 21, 2026, so this uses Vendr's buyer data instead. [8]

My Growth plan is $149 a month for up to 500,000 monthly active users. The Adjust contract buys attribution as well, which I don't sell, so if you need that, this isn't a like-for-like comparison.

## Switching from Adjust

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Keep Adjust for attribution if you still need it. DLN doesn't care.

## Questions

### How does Adjust's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Adjust bills on attributions. Its live pricing page refused automated requests on October 21, 2026, so this uses Vendr's buyer data instead. Vendr's median Adjust contract is $44,000 a year, about $3,670 a month, and the smallest it lists is $10,800 a year, about $900 a month. My Growth plan is $149 a month for up to 500,000 monthly active users. The Adjust contract buys attribution as well, which I don't sell, so if you need that, this isn't a like-for-like comparison.

### When is Adjust the better choice?

You buy ads and need attribution, including SKAdNetwork when users opt out of tracking. You ship games or less common platforms: Adjust has SDKs for Unity, Cocos2d-x, Steamworks, Windows and more.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Adjust?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Singular

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Singular is an attribution and marketing analytics platform. Its free plan includes deferred deep linking, which is more than some MMPs give away. The catch is in its own words: every Singular deep link is also an attribution link, made on its link page and carrying its tracking.

| | DeepLinkNow | Singular | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | Free: 15,000 paid conversions, deferred deep linking included, no card | [1] [7] |
| Paid plans | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Growth at $0.05 per conversion ("Let's Talk"). Enterprise by demo. | [1] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Growth and Enterprise | [1] [4] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created on the Create Link page as sng.link/<app id>/<link id>, with the target in _dl and _ddl. Every deep link is an attribution link. | [2] [3] |
| iOS clipboard handoff | The link page copies the link before the App Store, and the SDK reads it on first launch. A scored match is the backup. | Needs your own landing page with Singular's Web SDK and a download button | [5] |
| Deferred click window | 1 hour | 6 hours by default, 24 on request through your Customer Success Manager | [3] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | The iOS SDK's privacy manifest declares tracking, and it collects the IDFA when the user allows it | [6] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | singular.net on EasyPrivacy; its SDK and web SDK hosts on AdGuard Tracking Protection | [8] [9] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Singular if…

- You run paid user acquisition and want attribution, cost aggregation (Singular lists 1,200+ connectors), SKAdNetwork and fraud prevention, starting free.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

If most of your installs are organic, Singular's free plan may cover you for a long time, since it counts paid conversions. If you run ads and get 30,000 paid conversions a month, that's up to $1,500 a month on Growth at $0.05 each. An app with 100,000 monthly users is $49 a month on my Startup plan whatever it spends on ads, but you'd still need something else for attribution.

| | DeepLinkNow | Kochava | Sources |

# DeepLinkNow vs Airbridge

Mobile measurement platform (MMP). Facts as of October 19, 2026, each with a public source.

Airbridge is a mobile measurement platform with deep linking built in. It's cheaper than the big MMPs, but it's still an MMP: links get created up front, the SDK reads advertising IDs, and on iOS the deferred link can sit waiting for the user to answer the tracking prompt.

| | DeepLinkNow | Airbridge | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | None on the pricing page. Core is from $40/mo after a 30-day trial. | [1] [2] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users, one flat price per plan | Data points: 500K a month on Core, then $0.0001 each | [2] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created first, in the dashboard, Google Sheets or the API. Custom domains must be a dedicated subdomain. | [3] |
| Deferred link on iOS | Handed over on first launch. Nothing to wait for. | The SDK waits for the ATT answer (30 seconds by default) before delivering it | [4] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | IDFA and GAID collected by default | [5] |
| Ad-blocker lists | Not on any of them | SDK, attribution and event domains, plus a deferred-deeplink rule, on AdGuard's tracking list | [6] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No DeepLinkNow domain is on AdGuard or EasyPrivacy, so ad blockers don't stop the link page.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.

## Pick Airbridge if…

- You want a full MMP, with ad network integrations and attribution, at a lower entry price than AppsFlyer.

If you just need links that open the right screen after install, don't pay for the rest.

## The pricing math

Airbridge's Core plan starts at $40 a month for 500,000 data points, then $0.0001 per data point. Its pricing page (checked October 20, 2026) says $40 covers about 35,000 monthly active users at typical usage. [1] [2]

Take Airbridge's own figure: an app with 35,000 monthly users pays about $40 on Core. That's past my free plan (25,000), so on DeepLinkNow it's $49 on Startup. Airbridge is cheaper there, and includes attribution. Below 25,000 monthly users I'm free and Airbridge is still $40.

## Switching from Airbridge

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Airbridge SDK, and its ATT prompt if deep linking was its only job.

## Questions

### How does Airbridge's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Airbridge's Core plan starts at $40 a month for 500,000 data points, then $0.0001 per data point. Its pricing page (checked October 20, 2026) says $40 covers about 35,000 monthly active users at typical usage. Take Airbridge's own figure: an app with 35,000 monthly users pays about $40 on Core. That's past my free plan (25,000), so on DeepLinkNow it's $49 on Startup. Airbridge is cheaper there, and includes attribution. Below 25,000 monthly users I'm free and Airbridge is still $40.

### When is Airbridge the better choice?

You want a full MMP, with ad network integrations and attribution, at a lower entry price than AppsFlyer.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Airbridge?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Linkrunner

Low-cost mobile measurement platform. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Linkrunner is an attribution platform priced for startups, with deep links included. It costs a fraction of the big MMPs and its developer tooling is good. It's still an MMP: clicks carry advertising IDs, and the app gets attribution data rather than a score it can set a threshold on.

| | DeepLinkNow | Linkrunner | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | 25,000 attributed installs, deferred deep linking included, no card. Data kept 30 days. | [1] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users (devices that open your app with the SDK). Each distinct link path counts once toward the link limit (1,000 on the free plan). | Attributed installs: $0.010 each up to 50,000 a month, falling to $0.007 past 500,000 | [1] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Your subdomain with any query, like /product?variant_id=987, without a record per destination. Campaign links are created. | [3] |
| Link domain | yourapp.deeplinknow.com on every plan, your own domain from $49/mo | Your own subdomain, as a CNAME to api.linkrunner.io | [5] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | Clicks store GAID or IDFA and ad network click IDs. The Expo plugin adds the ATT prompt text unless you set disableIdfa. | [4] [7] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | The deep link and campaign data (organic or not). No confidence score. | [6] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Published prices: $0, $49 or $149 a month. You only talk to me if you want Enterprise.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.
- Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace on Enterprise.

## Pick Linkrunner if…

- You also want install attribution for Meta, Google, Apple Search Ads and SKAdNetwork from one SDK, at about a cent per install.
- You want its tooling: an MCP server that checks your link setup, an lr doctor CLI for CI, and a hand-off page for social in-app browsers.
- You need Capacitor, Cordova or Unity SDKs.

Sources: [1] [8] [9] [10] [11]

If you don't need attribution, you don't need the advertising IDs that come with it.

## The pricing math

Linkrunner bills on attributed installs: 25,000 free, then $0.010 to $0.007 each depending on volume. It also lists a deep-links-only price ($24 a month billed yearly, or $30 monthly in its FAQ) that isn't on the main pricing page. [1] [2]

At $0.009 to $0.010 per install, 100,000 attributed installs in a month comes to roughly $900 to $1,000. I don't count installs: an app with 100,000 monthly users is $49 on Startup. Under 25,000 installs a month both are free, and if you need the attribution, Linkrunner is the cheapest MMP on this list.

## Switching from Linkrunner

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Linkrunner SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does Linkrunner's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Linkrunner bills on attributed installs: 25,000 free, then $0.010 to $0.007 each depending on volume. You want its tooling: an MCP server that checks your link setup, an lr doctor CLI for CI, and a hand-off page for social in-app browsers. You need Capacitor, Cordova or Unity SDKs.

# DeepLinkNow vs Detour

Deferred deep linking for React Native and Expo. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Detour is the closest thing to what I built: deferred deep links for React Native and Expo without an attribution suite. Software Mansion makes it, Expo's blog ran its guest post in July 2026, and its Expo Router support is good, including a pattern for holding a link until the user gets past your sign-in screen. The differences are the free plan, what you pay for, and how much the app learns about a match.

| | DeepLinkNow | Detour | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | 1,500 clicks a month and 50 short links per app. Past the limit, deep link matching stops and plain redirects keep working. | [1] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users (devices that open your app with the SDK). Each distinct link path counts once toward the link limit (1,000 on the free plan). | Link clicks: Starter $19/mo for 70,000, Scale $79/mo for 350,000, then optional pay-as-you-go per 1,000 clicks | [1] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Scale, $79/mo. Free and Starter links live on a .godetour.link subdomain. | [1] [4] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Any path and query after the app's fixed /<app_hash>/ segment, which stays in the URL on a custom domain too | [2] [4] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | A link, or nothing. The server applies its own threshold (850 by default, 700 to 1200) and sends no score. | [3] [4] |
| Match window | 1 hour | 15 minutes by default, configurable from 5 to 180 | [3] |
| Expo Router | A +native-intent helper (@deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router) and a useDeferredDeepLink() hook | A +native-intent handler and a DetourProvider, with examples that keep the link through sign-in | [4] [6] |
| How long click data is kept | A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days. | The privacy policy says data is kept "as long as needed to provide" the service and gives no period | [7] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block list checkers, no sign-up needed.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Detour if…

- You'd rather depend on Software Mansion, a well-known React Native company, and want SDKs that are MIT-licensed on GitHub.
- You want smart banners, a hand-off out of the Instagram and Facebook in-app browsers, or scheduled analytics exports. I don't do those.
- Your app has more than 25,000 monthly users but your links get under 70,000 clicks a month: Starter at $19 costs less than my Startup plan.

Sources: [5] [4] [1]

If you want a free plan sized for a real launch and a score you can set your own threshold on, try mine first.

## The pricing math

Detour bills on link clicks: 1,500 free, 70,000 for $19, 350,000 for $79. I bill on monthly active users, the devices that open your app with the SDK. The two don't convert one to one, so it depends on how many clicks each user makes. [1]

Say 15,000 people use your app each month and your links get 40,000 clicks across a few hundred paths. Detour: Starter, $19. DeepLinkNow: free. Now say 60,000 monthly users and the same 40,000 clicks: Detour is still $19, and I'm $49 on Startup. If your users far outnumber your link clicks, Detour costs less.

## Switching from Detour

1. Add the DLN SDK next to Detour's and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work without the /<app_hash>/ segment.
3. Swap createDetourNativeIntentHandler for createRedirectSystemPath from @deeplinknow/react-native/expo-router, and DetourProvider's link for useDeferredDeepLink().
4. Keep Detour until the links you've already shared stop getting clicks. Its custom-domain links stop resolving when the subscription ends.

## Questions

### How does Detour's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Detour bills on link clicks: 1,500 free, 70,000 for $19, 350,000 for $79. I bill on monthly active users, the devices that open your app with the SDK. The two don't convert one to one, so it depends on how many clicks each user makes. Say 15,000 people use your app each month and your links get 40,000 clicks across a few hundred paths. Detour: Starter, $19. DeepLinkNow: free. Now say 60,000 monthly users and the same 40,000 clicks: Detour is still $19, and I'm $49 on Startup. If your users far outnumber your link clicks, Detour costs less.

### When is Detour the better choice?

You'd rather depend on Software Mansion, a well-known React Native company, and want SDKs that are MIT-licensed on GitHub. You want smart banners, a hand-off out of the Instagram and Facebook in-app browsers, or scheduled analytics exports. I don't do those. Your app has more than 25,000 monthly users but your links get under 70,000 clicks a month: Starter at $19 costs less than my Startup plan.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Detour?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

## Sources

1. [Detour: billing](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/fundamentals/billing)
2. [Detour: click handling](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/architecture/click-handling)
3. [Detour: matching](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/platform/architecture/matching)
4. [Detour docs (full text)](https://detour.swmansion.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
5. [Detour React Native SDK](https://github.com/software-mansion-labs/react-native-detour)
6. [Expo blog: deferred deep linking the right way](https://expo.dev/blog/deferred-deep-linking-the-right-way)
7. [Detour privacy policy](https://godetour.dev/privacy-policy)

# DeepLinkNow vs ChottuLink

Deep linking with install attribution. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

ChottuLink prices the way I do, by monthly active users, and its paid plans are cheaper than mine. The differences are in how links work, what the app learns about a match, and the attribution features it's adding, such as lead and conversion tracking.

| | DeepLinkNow | ChottuLink | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | Free to 25,000 MAU on a chottu.link subdomain, with deferred deep links. MAU means users who opened the app in the last 30 days. | [1] |
| Paid plans | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Indie $19/mo to 75,000 MAU, Growth $39/mo to 150,000, Scale $99/mo to 500,000 | [1] [2] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Growth, $39/mo, on the plan cards. Other text on the same page says the free plan includes one; the cards say it doesn't. | [1] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created first, in the dashboard, the SDK's link builder or the REST API. Each path can only be used once on a domain. | [3] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | matchFound (true or false) and an attribution type. No score. | [4] |
| Attribution | None. Forward the link to your own analytics. | Lead and conversion tracking with revenue; Meta and Google Conversions API on Enterprise | [4] [1] |
| Flutter SDK licence | Flutter SDK (pub.dev `deeplinknow`), MIT-licensed | Proprietary EULA, for active subscribers only | [5] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block list checkers, no sign-up needed.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.
- Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace on Enterprise.

## Pick ChottuLink if…

- You're past 25,000 monthly users and price decides it: Indie is $19 for up to 75,000, and Growth is $39 with a custom domain. Both cost less than mine.
- You need Unity, Capacitor or web SDKs, webhooks, or lead and conversion tracking.

Sources: [1] [4] [6]

If you want any path to work as a link and a score you can set a threshold on, try mine.

## The pricing math

ChottuLink and I count nearly the same thing: users who opened the app (ChottuLink over the last 30 days, me over the calendar month). So the plans compare directly. [1]

At 20,000 monthly users both are free. At 60,000, ChottuLink is $19 and I'm $49. At 140,000, ChottuLink is $39 with a custom domain and I'm $149 (Startup stops at 100,000). ChottuLink is cheaper at every paid step.

## Switching from ChottuLink

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the ChottuLink SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does ChottuLink's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

ChottuLink and I count nearly the same thing: users who opened the app (ChottuLink over the last 30 days, me over the calendar month). So the plans compare directly. At 20,000 monthly users both are free. At 60,000, ChottuLink is $19 and I'm $49. At 140,000, ChottuLink is $39 with a custom domain and I'm $149 (Startup stops at 100,000). ChottuLink is cheaper at every paid step.

### When is ChottuLink the better choice?

You're past 25,000 monthly users and price decides it: Indie is $19 for up to 75,000, and Growth is $39 with a custom domain. Both cost less than mine. You need Unity, Capacitor or web SDKs, webhooks, or lead and conversion tracking.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to ChottuLink?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs WarpLink

Deep linking with attribution and analytics. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

WarpLink is a well-built small deep linking service with more developer tooling than I have: an MCP server, nine free checkers and generators, an OpenAPI spec and published accuracy numbers. It returns a confidence score, like I do. It bills per click, creates links up front and has no clipboard step on iOS.

| | DeepLinkNow | WarpLink | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | 10,000 tracked clicks and 100 links, with a custom domain for the first 90 days | [1] |
| What you pay for | Monthly active users (devices that open your app with the SDK). Each distinct link path counts once toward the link limit (1,000 on the free plan). | Tracked clicks: $19 for 100,000, $49 for 500,000, $99 for 2 million, $149 unlimited. Redirects keep working over the cap. | [1] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created first, per app, on {handle}.aplnk.to | [2] [7] |
| Deferred link on iOS | The link page copies the link before the App Store, and the SDK reads it on first launch. A scored match is the backup. | No clipboard step. A probabilistic match on IP address, language and time zone, held 6 hours by default. | [3] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | A score from 0.0 to 1.0; 1.0 for an install-referrer match on Android | [3] |
| How long click data is kept | A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days. | 90 days to 3 years, depending on the plan | [4] |
| Where data lives | Sydney: Vercel's syd1 region and a database in AWS ap-southeast-2. Custom domains are served through Cloudflare. | A database in the United States (Northern Virginia) | [5] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.
- Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace on Enterprise.

## Pick WarpLink if…

- You want the tooling: an MCP server with 34 tools, nine free checkers and generators, an OpenAPI spec and published accuracy numbers.
- Your app has many users but few link clicks: Starter is $19 for 100,000 clicks.
- You want everything unlimited for a flat $149 a month.

Sources: [6] [8] [9] [1]

If most of your users are on iPhones, the clipboard handoff is worth testing before you decide.

## The pricing math

WarpLink bills on tracked clicks, one per link and visitor address in 24 hours. I bill on monthly active users. [1]

An app with 60,000 monthly users and 80,000 tracked clicks a month: WarpLink Starter, $19, and DeepLinkNow Startup, $49. An app with 20,000 users running a campaign that gets 150,000 clicks: WarpLink Growth, $49, and DeepLinkNow free. Which is cheaper depends on clicks per user.

## Switching from WarpLink

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the WarpLink SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does WarpLink's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

WarpLink bills on tracked clicks, one per link and visitor address in 24 hours. I bill on monthly active users. An app with 60,000 monthly users and 80,000 tracked clicks a month: WarpLink Starter, $19, and DeepLinkNow Startup, $49. An app with 20,000 users running a campaign that gets 150,000 clicks: WarpLink Growth, $49, and DeepLinkNow free. Which is cheaper depends on clicks per user.

### When is WarpLink the better choice?

You want the tooling: an MCP server with 34 tools, nine free checkers and generators, an OpenAPI spec and published accuracy numbers. Your app has many users but few link clicks: Starter is $19 for 100,000 clicks. You want everything unlimited for a flat $149 a month.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to WarpLink?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs Dynalinks

Deep linking with Firebase-style links. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Dynalinks is a small, cheap deep linking service that took the Firebase Dynamic Links long-link format seriously. For a single app its paid plan costs less than mine. Its free plan doesn't do deferred deep links at all.

| | DeepLinkNow | Dynalinks | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | Basic: 100 links per project, no deferred deep linking | [1] [2] |
| Cheapest plan with deferred deep links | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Pro, $14.99 per project per month, unlimited links | [2] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | Pro, one per project. Links on it stop resolving if the project drops back to Basic. | [3] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Named links are created in the console or the API and looked up by path. Firebase-style ?link= long links work on Pro. | [4] [8] |
| Match window on iOS | 1 hour | 10 minutes, single use | [5] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | A high, medium or low label and a 0 to 100 score | [6] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | Not used. No ATT prompt. | [7] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.
- Free AASA, assetlinks.json and ad-block list checkers, no sign-up needed.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick Dynalinks if…

- You have one app and want the lowest price with a custom domain: Pro is $14.99 a month.
- You're moving Firebase long links and want to change only the host. Dynalinks reads more of the Firebase parameters than I do, including the fallback ones I ignore.

Sources: [2] [4]

If you want deferred deep links without paying first, and any path to work, try mine.

## The pricing math

Dynalinks bills per project: Basic is free with 100 links and no deferred links, and Pro is $14.99 a month per project with unlimited links. It doesn't meter clicks or users. [2]

One app with 40,000 monthly users: Dynalinks Pro, $14.99, and DeepLinkNow Startup, $49. Two apps: $29.98 against $49, since Startup covers 3 apps. Under 25,000 monthly users I'm free with deferred links included, and Dynalinks needs Pro for them.

## Switching from Dynalinks

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Dynalinks SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does Dynalinks's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Dynalinks bills per project: Basic is free with 100 links and no deferred links, and Pro is $14.99 a month per project with unlimited links. It doesn't meter clicks or users. One app with 40,000 monthly users: Dynalinks Pro, $14.99, and DeepLinkNow Startup, $49. Two apps: $29.98 against $49, since Startup covers 3 apps. Under 25,000 monthly users I'm free with deferred links included, and Dynalinks needs Pro for them.

### When is Dynalinks the better choice?

You have one app and want the lowest price with a custom domain: Pro is $14.99 a month. You're moving Firebase long links and want to change only the host. Dynalinks reads more of the Firebase parameters than I do, including the fallback ones I ignore.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Dynalinks?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

| | DeepLinkNow | Flinku | Sources |

# DeepLinkNow vs Rift

Deep linking and attribution API. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

Rift is a new deep linking and attribution API, aimed at developers and AI agents. It's inexpensive and includes a custom domain on the free plan. Deferral is clipboard and install referrer only, and the SDKs are native iOS, Android and web.

| | DeepLinkNow | Rift | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | 50 links and 10,000 events a month, one custom domain, deferred deep linking | [1] |
| Paid plans | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Pro $18/mo (2,000 links, 100,000 events), Business $55/mo, Scale $199/mo. Hard limits, no overage. | [1] |
| Making links | Any path on your domain is already a link. Nothing to create. | Created first, with POST /v1/links | [3] |
| Deferred matching | The link page copies the link before the App Store, and the SDK reads it on first launch. A scored match is the backup. | Clipboard on iOS and install referrer on Android. No fingerprint fallback is documented, so a refused paste means no match. | [2] |
| SDKs | iOS, Android, React Native (with Expo) and a Flutter SDK (pub.dev `deeplinknow`), plus an MCP server | iOS, Android and a web SDK, plus an MCP server and a CLI. No React Native or Flutter SDK in the docs. | [5] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | One on the free plan. It's what enables Universal Links and App Links. | [1] [4] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- Native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) SDKs, a Flutter SDK (pub.dev `deeplinknow`), a React Native SDK with an Expo config plugin, an Expo Router helper and a useDeferredDeepLink() hook, and an MCP server so coding agents can set it up.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- No attribution, no advertising IDs, no ATT prompt. A deferred link can be claimed for 1 hour after the click, and stored fingerprints are deleted within 30 days.

## Pick Rift if…

- You want a custom domain on a free plan, or a $18 paid tier, and you're fine creating each link.
- You're building for AI agents: Rift resolves links as JSON and ships an MCP server and a CLI.

Sources: [1] [5]

If you ship React Native, or need a backup when iOS users refuse the paste, try mine.

## The pricing math

Rift bills on links and events: 50 links and 10,000 events free, 2,000 links and 100,000 events for $18. Its pricing doesn't define an event. [1]

An app that needs 500 links is on Rift Pro at $18. On DeepLinkNow, 500 distinct paths fit the free plan while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users, then it's $49. Past my free plan, Rift is cheaper.

## Switching from Rift

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the Rift SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does Rift's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

Rift bills on links and events: 50 links and 10,000 events free, 2,000 links and 100,000 events for $18. Its pricing doesn't define an event. An app that needs 500 links is on Rift Pro at $18. On DeepLinkNow, 500 distinct paths fit the free plan while the app stays under 25,000 monthly users, then it's $49. Past my free plan, Rift is cheaper.

### When is Rift the better choice?

You want a custom domain on a free plan, or a $18 paid tier, and you're fine creating each link. You're building for AI agents: Rift resolves links as JSON and ships an MCP server and a CLI.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to Rift?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

# DeepLinkNow vs LinkTrace

Install attribution and referral links over REST. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

LinkTrace is a REST API for install attribution and referral links, with no SDK to add. It's cheap and says it's privacy-first. It matches by fingerprint only, and Universal Links and App Links are on its top plan.

| | DeepLinkNow | LinkTrace | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | 100 links and 1,000 attributed installs, once. Paid plans refresh monthly. | [1] |
| Paid plans | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Growth $9.99/mo (1,000 links, 10,000 installs), Scale $29.99/mo (unlimited) | [1] |
| Universal Links and App Links | Every plan, on yourapp.deeplinknow.com or your own domain | Scale only, on a yourbrand.linktrace.in subdomain | [1] [2] |
| Deferred matching | The link page copies the link before the App Store, and the SDK reads it on first launch. A scored match is the backup. | Fingerprint only, for 24 hours. No install referrer. The result is attributed true or false. | [2] |
| SDK | iOS, Android, React Native (with Expo) and a Flutter SDK (pub.dev `deeplinknow`) | None. A REST API with copy-paste examples. | [3] |
| Advertising IDs | Never read. No ATT prompt. | Not used | [2] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- iOS clipboard handoff on every plan: the link page copies the link and the SDK reads it on first launch.
- Native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) SDKs, a Flutter SDK (pub.dev `deeplinknow`), a React Native SDK with an Expo config plugin, an Expo Router helper and a useDeferredDeepLink() hook, and an MCP server so coding agents can set it up.
- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.
- Hosted in Sydney (Vercel syd1, database in AWS ap-southeast-2), if that matters to your users or your lawyers.

## Pick LinkTrace if…

- You don't want an SDK in the app, and fingerprint matching alone is enough.
- You want referral tracking with referrer IDs for $9.99 a month.

Sources: [3] [1] [2]

If you want the install referrer on Android and the clipboard on iOS, which are exact when they work, try mine.

## The pricing math

LinkTrace bills flat per plan on links and attributed installs: $9.99 for 10,000 installs a month, $29.99 unlimited. I bill on monthly active users. [1]

20,000 installs a month with Universal Links: LinkTrace Scale, $29.99. On DeepLinkNow it depends on monthly users: free at 20,000, $49 at 60,000. Below 25,000 users I'm free; above it LinkTrace is cheaper.

## Switching from LinkTrace

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the LinkTrace SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does LinkTrace's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

LinkTrace bills flat per plan on links and attributed installs: $9.99 for 10,000 installs a month, $29.99 unlimited. I bill on monthly active users. 20,000 installs a month with Universal Links: LinkTrace Scale, $29.99. On DeepLinkNow it depends on monthly users: free at 20,000, $49 at 60,000. Below 25,000 users I'm free; above it LinkTrace is cheaper.

### When is LinkTrace the better choice?

You don't want an SDK in the app, and fingerprint matching alone is enough. You want referral tracking with referrer IDs for $9.99 a month.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to LinkTrace?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

## Sources

1. [LinkTrace pricing](https://linktrace.in/pricing/)
2. [LinkTrace llms.txt](https://linktrace.in/llms.txt)
3. [LinkTrace FAQ](https://linktrace.in/faq/)
4. [LinkTrace API reference](https://linktrace.in/documentation/api-reference/)

# DeepLinkNow vs AppsOnAir

App platform with an AppLink deep linking module. Facts as of October 21, 2026, each with a public source.

AppsOnAir sells CodePush, app distribution and push, and AppLink is its deep linking module. It has a real Firebase importer that reads Google Takeout exports. There's no AppLink on the free plan, and the custom domain is an add-on.

| | DeepLinkNow | AppsOnAir | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free plan | Free up to 25,000 monthly active users, deferred deep links included. No card. | No AppLink on the free plan | [1] |
| Cheapest plan with deep links | $0, $49 or $149 a month, published, billed monthly. Enterprise from $500 a month | Pro with AppLink only, $34.98/mo, as the pricing calculator showed it. Other prices printed on the same page disagree. | [1] |
| Custom domain | $49/mo (Startup) | An add-on, $19.99/mo | [1] |
| Deferred window | 1 hour | 1 hour by default; longer windows depend on the plan | [2] |
| What the app gets | A confidence score from 0 to 100 and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label. You pick the threshold. | Organic or non-organic. No score. | [2] |
| Firebase links | No importer. FDL-style long links on your domain hand the app the link parameter. | Imports Google Takeout CSV exports of your Firebase links | [3] |

## Where DeepLinkNow is ahead

- A free plan up to 25,000 monthly active users, with deferred deep links and no card.
- Published prices: $0, $49 or $149 a month. You only talk to me if you want Enterprise.
- Your own domain from $49 a month on Startup, set up in the dashboard.
- Every fingerprint match comes back with a 0 to 100 score and a HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW label, so you decide what to trust.
- Any path on your link domain is already a link, with no prefix and nothing to create first.

## Pick AppsOnAir if…

- You're leaving Firebase with a large Takeout export and want it imported.
- You already use AppsOnAir for CodePush or push and want one vendor.

Sources: [3] [1]

If deep links are all you need, you don't need the bundle around them.

## The pricing math

AppsOnAir prices AppLink as a module on a base plan: Pro is $9.99 plus $24.99 for AppLink (50,000 app links), Pro Plus is $24.99 plus $49.99 (250,000). [1]

One app with a custom domain: $34.98 plus $19.99, so $54.97 a month on AppsOnAir, and $49 on DeepLinkNow. If you already pay AppsOnAir for another module, AppLink adds $24.99 plus the domain.

## Switching from AppsOnAir

1. Add the DLN SDK next to the one you have and ship it.
2. Point your link domain at DLN. Paths on it work straight away.
3. Read the link with checkDeferredDeepLink() on first launch.
4. Remove the AppsOnAir SDK once the links you've already shared stop getting clicks.

## Questions

### How does AppsOnAir's pricing compare with DeepLinkNow's?

AppsOnAir prices AppLink as a module on a base plan: Pro is $9.99 plus $24.99 for AppLink (50,000 app links), Pro Plus is $24.99 plus $49.99 (250,000). One app with a custom domain: $34.98 plus $19.99, so $54.97 a month on AppsOnAir, and $49 on DeepLinkNow. If you already pay AppsOnAir for another module, AppLink adds $24.99 plus the domain.

### When is AppsOnAir the better choice?

You're leaving Firebase with a large Takeout export and want it imported. You already use AppsOnAir for CodePush or push and want one vendor.

### Can I run DeepLinkNow next to AppsOnAir?

Yes. The SDK doesn't depend on any other deep linking SDK, so you can ship both, move your link domain over, and remove the old one later.

## Sources

1. [AppsOnAir pricing](https://www.appsonair.com/plans-pricing)
2. [AppsOnAir AppLink overview](https://documentation.appsonair.com/MobileQuickstart/AppLink/overview.html)
3. [AppsOnAir AppLink FAQs](https://documentation.appsonair.com/MobileQuickstart/AppLink/applink-faqs.html)
